mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares bulk stress with longitudinal and tangential stresses in a solid subjected to hydrostatic pressure?

options.A: Bulk stress is equal to the normal stress acting equally in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the axis of the applied force and tangential stress acts parallel to the surface.
options.B: Bulk stress is always larger than longitudinal stress for the same applied force.
options.C: Bulk stress is a shear stress that acts on planes parallel to the applied force.
options.D: Bulk stress exists only in fluids and not in solid materials.

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress is equal to the normal stress acting equally in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the axis of the applied force and tangential stress acts parallel to the surface.
mcqs.explanation: In hydrostatic conditions the internal restoring force per unit area (bulk stress) is the same on every face of the solid, i.e., it is isotropic normal stress. Longitudinal stress is normal stress directed along the line of an applied axial force, and tangential (shear) stress acts parallel to the surface. Options B, C and D describe incorrect relationships.

mcqs.question: In a circular shaft of radius r subjected to a torque T, the tangential (shear) stress τ on the surface is given by which expression?
mcqs.explanation: For a solid circular shaft the torsional shear stress at a radius r is τ = T·r / J, where J = π r⁴ /2 is the polar moment of inertia. This formula is standard for torsion problems in competitive exams. Options A, B and D are algebraically incorrect forms.

mcqs.question: In the context of mechanical properties of solids, stress is defined as:

options.A: Force per unit volume acting internally
options.B: Force per unit area acting internally

mcqs.answer: Force per unit area acting internally
mcqs.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit area within a material when it is subjected to external loads. It is not related to volume, displacement, or energy per mass, making options A, C, and D incorrect.

mcqs.question: A force of 200 N is applied uniformly on a cross‑sectional area of 0.05 m² of a metal rod. What is the magnitude of the normal stress in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Stress = Force / Area = 200 N / 0.05 m² = 4,000 N/m² = 4,000 Pa. The other options result from incorrect division or misplaced decimal points.

mcqs.question: How does longitudinal stress differ from bulk stress in a solid?

options.A: Longitudinal stress acts along the direction of the applied force, while bulk stress acts equally in all directions.
options.B: Longitudinal stress is a shear stress, whereas bulk stress is a normal stress.
options.C: Longitudinal stress occurs only in fluids, while bulk stress occurs only in solids.
options.D: Both stresses are identical and interchangeable terms.

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal stress acts along the direction of the applied force, while bulk stress acts equally in all directions.
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal (or normal) stress is directed along the axis of an applied axial load. Bulk stress, also called hydrostatic stress, is isotropic—it is the same normal stress on all faces of the material. Options B, C, and D mischaracterize the nature of the stresses.

mcqs.question: A cube of material is placed in a chamber where a uniform pressure of 5×10⁶ N/m² is applied from all sides. What is the bulk stress experienced by the cube?
mcqs.explanation: Bulk stress under hydrostatic pressure equals the applied pressure because the normal stress is the same on every face. Hence the bulk stress is 5×10⁶ N/m². The other values are unrelated to the definition.

mcqs.question: A rectangular block of dimensions 0.2 m × 0.1 m has a horizontal force of 300 N applied on its top surface, causing it to slide over the bottom surface. What is the tangential (shear) stress on the bottom surface?
mcqs.explanation: Contact area = 0.2 m × 0.1 m = 0.02 m². Shear (tangential) stress = Force / Area = 300 N / 0.02 m² = 15,000 N/m² = 15,000 Pa. Options A, C, and D correspond to incorrect area or force values.

mcqs.question: A steel rod of length 1.5 m and cross‑sectional area 2×10⁻⁴ m² is pulled by a force of 500 N. According to the definition of stress, what is the stress in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Stress = Force / Area = 500 N / (2×10⁻⁴ m²) = 2.5×10⁶ N/m² = 2.5×10⁶ Pa. The other options arise from misplaced decimal placement.
